transfers.source_mechanism: Flow rate enables structural adaptation under feedback constraints, producing optimized network topology
transfers.target_problem: A mid-sized city (population 800,000) has a traffic signal network with 247 signalized intersections. The current signal timing plan is optimized centrally every 6 months using a macroscopic traffic model, but it cannot adapt to real-time conditions: incidents, weather, special events, and construction. Re-optimizing centrally every minute is computationally infeasible and would require expensive predictive models. The city wants a distributed, adaptive signal timing approach that uses only local traffic flow measurements (vehicle count and queue length at each intersection) to adjust green-split and offset in real time, without a central optimizer.
transfers.transferred_principle: Traffic flow enables signal timing adaptation under local feedback constraints, producing optimized traffic network throughput
transfers.required_translation: Replace rhythmic contraction/thickening/thinning with signal green phase extension/reduction; replace tube radius with green time allocation; replace resource flow with vehicle flow; replace structural integrity with minimum green time constraints
transfers.expected_effect: Distributed adaptive signal timing that optimizes traffic flow without central coordination
transfers.testable_prediction: Under incident conditions, the adaptive network will reduce average intersection delay by at least 15% compared to the fixed-timing system within 30 minutes of the incident, while maintaining stability without oscillations
